title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Lawn and turf care
audience: Lawn and turf operators, including solo operators, who are starting or growing a mowing and maintenance round.
learningOutcomes: Write a lawn offer with a clear promised result, a visit schedule, conditions and a return-visit guarantee
Identify the friction and risk a lawn client carries and reduce them
Price a lawn offer on value and on cost, and check it against the sourced market range

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will mow your lawn' is a service. 'I will mow and edge your lawn every fortnight, leave the paths clear of clippings, and come back within two working days to re-mow any strip I missed' is an offer. The client buys a lawn that looks the same after each visit, on a known schedule, with a fix if a visit falls short. The two-day return window is example wording; set your own window from your round records.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome (lawn height and edge line after each visit); a time frame (the visit day and the season the plan runs); the work the client must do (open the gate, move pet bowls, say if the lawn is wet or a sprinkler is running); the certainty you provide (a visit checklist and a photo at sign-off, taken with the client's consent); and the risk you carry (the return visit). Keep each part checkable. Put scope and exclusions in writing. In Western Australia a quote becomes binding once accepted (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). In Victoria a contract exists whether the agreement was verbal or written (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 9 July 2025), so the exclusions must be in the offer, not only in your head. List any gardens, hard edges or areas that are not mowed.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make booking, access and handover simple. Record gate codes, the tap location and any pets once, on the client record, and send the visit day in one message. Fewer decisions for the client usually allow a higher price, because the client pays for reliability and convenience. Watering is part of the handover. In Victoria, a watering system may run only between 6 pm and 10 am (Victorian Government, water.vic.gov.au, updated 13 January 2026). In NSW, Sydney Water limits sprinklers and hoses to before 10 am or after 4 pm, and check the rule for the utility that serves the client's address.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees for services apply and cannot be removed by contract. Victorian guidance says a tradesperson guarantees due care and skill, fitness for any specified purpose, and completion within a reasonable time where no time is set (Consumer Affairs Victoria). A 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra on top of those rights. Do not state a measurable result, such as a greener lawn in four weeks, unless you can show evidence for it. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Packages that step up in price
instruction.body: Three tiers suit a lawn round. Good: a fortnightly mow and edge. Better: the same, plus a visual check of the sprinkler heads and a short note of any fault at each visit. Best: the same, plus a monthly photo report and one extra visit in the peak growing months. Price each tier from your own cost per productive hour, not from a copied rate. Market reference: the Melbourne cost guide lists a fortnightly plan for a medium lawn (100 to 250 m²) at $63, $79 and $125 per visit, GST included (What's the Damage, updated November 2026). Jobber describes stepped packages in which each higher level adds something the customer can see (published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). State one total for each tier and say whether GST is included, as Western Australian guidance asks (WA Consumer Protection).

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check against your cost and time. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). A higher price is justified when the client can see the result, the certainty and the time saved. If the cost-based price sits above the sourced range, check the standard mowing time and the scope before adding a premium.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a client would repeat, such as 'the lawn is cut and edged on the same day each fortnight'.
Set a visit schedule you have checked against your own round records, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, such as opening the gate and clearing pet waste, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a visit checklist and a photo at sign-off, with consent.
Decide the return-visit guarantee and check that you can afford it.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost and time and against the sourced range.

workedExamples.situation: A lawn operator quotes an hourly rate and loses fortnightly work to cheaper quotes. Clients say they cannot tell what each visit will include.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer as a package and decide how to price it.
workedExamples.reasoning: A fixed-scope fortnightly package with a visit checklist, a sign-off photo and a re-mow window for missed strips gives the client certainty that an hourly quote does not. The price is built from the operator's own cost per productive hour, then checked against the sourced Melbourne medium-lawn plan range of $63 to $125 per visit, GST included. The comparison uses the same GST basis as the quote. If the cost-based price is above that range, the operator checks the mowing standard time and the scope before deciding on a premium.

equipmentAndPpe: Visit checklist with photo sign-off, taken with consent
Client record for gate, water and pet details

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to something you control, such as a return visit within a window you have costed.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured and can show, such as photos taken at sign-off.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a plan price without saying whether GST is included
commonErrors.prevention: State one total for each tier and say whether GST is included.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state rules before acting.

Watering rules are set by state and by utility. Victoria: watering systems may run only between 6 pm and 10 am. NSW (Sydney Water): sprinklers and hoses before 10 am or after 4 pm, with a business exemption for landscaping services using drinking water. Check the rule for the state and utility where you work before promising a watering schedule.

No licence rule for mowing was found for Victoria. This does not confirm that no licence applies in any state. Pesticide and herbicide use is not confirmed for gardeners in Victoria, so this lesson does not offer chemical treatment in any package.

qualityStandard: Every lawn offer is written, states its exclusions and says whether GST is included.
Each tier price is built from the operator's own costs and checked against the sourced range.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with the outcome, schedule, exclusions and return-visit terms
Visit checklist and sign-off photo record, with consent
Price worksheet showing cost, margin and the market check
summary: A good lawn offer promises a repeatable result, a schedule, certainty and a fair return visit.
Higher rates follow from clearer value, not from longer hours.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a lawn offer does the customer buy?
What should a return-visit guarantee on a lawn round be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.covers: Western Australia only. Says a quote is a total amount that binds once accepted, an estimate can change, and the total including GST should be shown. Not a Victorian or NSW rule.
